source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The minimum normal urine output for an adult is about:
questions.rationale: Kidneys form roughly 30–60 mL per hour (about 1,500 mL/day); less than 30 mL/hour should be reported.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 15 Kidney physiology (PDF p. 483)
questions.quote: the kidneys form 0.5 to I ml. per minute, or 30 to 60 mls per hour

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Women get urinary tract infections more often than men mainly because they have:
questions.rationale: The short female urethra lets colonic bacteria (mostly E. coli) reach the bladder easily.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 15 UTI (PDF p. 493)
questions.quote: Females are at high risk to develop UTI because of short urethra

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The organism that most often causes urinary tract infection is:
questions.rationale: Colonic bacteria, especially E. coli, cause most UTIs; Klebsiella, Proteus and Pseudomonas also occur.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 15 UTI (PDF p. 493)
questions.quote: The most common etiologic agents are the colonic bacteria, specifically Escherichia coli.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After cystoscopy, the client has pink-tinged urine and mild burning. The nurse:
questions.rationale: Mucosal irritation causes pink urine and dysuria for 24–48 hours; push fluids and report bright bleeding, clots or retention.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 15 Cystoscopy (PDF p. 486)
questions.quote: Pink- tinged urine is normal (24-48 hrs).

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Before an intravenous pyelogram, the nurse's priority assessment is:
questions.rationale: IVP uses iodinated contrast; ask about allergy and keep epinephrine ready for anaphylaxis.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 15 IVP (PDF p. 486)
questions.quote: Prepare Epinephrine at bed side. Anaphylactic shock is a potential complication.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After an IVP, the client is encouraged to drink more fluids in order to:
questions.rationale: Fluids help excrete the dye and protect the kidneys; also watch for delayed allergic reactions.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 15 IVP (PDF p. 486)
questions.quote: Increase fluid intake to excrete the dye.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Before an ultrasound of the bladder, the nurse instructs the client to:
questions.rationale: A full bladder improves the image, so the client drinks water and holds urine.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 15 Ultrasound (PDF p. 488)
questions.quote: Distend the bladder (give 2 glosses of vsater). Illis permits better imaging.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The main complication the nurse watches for after a kidney biopsy is:
questions.rationale: The kidney is very vascular; keep bed rest for 24 hours, monitor VS and recheck Hct and Hgb.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 15 Renal biopsy (PDF p. 488)
questions.quote: Bleeding is the most common complication of the procedure.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: During the oliguric phase of acute kidney injury, the nurse expects:
questions.rationale: Oliguria raises BUN, creatinine, potassium, magnesium and phosphate, with acidosis and edema.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 15 Acute renal failure (PDF p. 489)
questions.quote: increased BUN, serum creatinine; edema; hypertension; hyperkalemia

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client recovering from acute kidney injury now passes 4 L of urine a day. The nurse monitors closely for:
questions.rationale: In the diuretic phase large urine volumes cause potassium loss and fluid deficit.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 15 Acute renal failure (PDF p. 489)
questions.quote: There is increased urine output (3 to 5 Vday), with excessive loss of potassium (hypokalemia).

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Severe anemia in chronic kidney disease is mainly due to:
questions.rationale: Damaged kidneys make less erythropoietin; epoetin alfa is given (watch for hypertension).
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 15 Chronic renal failure (PDF p. 489)
questions.quote: Decreased erythropoietin secretion reduces red blood cells production by the bone marrow.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on epoetin alfa for kidney disease should be monitored mainly for:
questions.rationale: Hypertension is the major side effect of epoetin alfa.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 15 CRF drugs (PDF p. 491)
questions.quote: Major side effect of Epogen Alfa is hypertension.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Why does chronic kidney disease cause low calcium and weak bones?
options: The kidneys cannot activate vitamin D
Too much calcium in the diet
questions.rationale: Without active vitamin D, calcium absorption falls; phosphate rises and renal osteodystrophy develops.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 15 Chronic renal failure (PDF p. 490)
questions.quote: Hypocalcemia. 'Illis is due to decreased calcium absorption caused by decreased vitamin D.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with chronic kidney disease is prescribed a phosphate binder. It should be taken:
questions.rationale: Phosphate binders such as aluminum hydroxide bind dietary phosphate in the gut, so they are taken with meals.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 15 CRF drugs (PDF p. 491)
questions.quote: a phosphate binder (to be administered with meals to prevent GI irritation).

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which over-the-counter drug should a client with chronic kidney disease avoid?
questions.rationale: Magnesium-containing products build up when the kidneys fail and can cause magnesium toxicity.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 15 CRF nursing care (PDF p. 491)
questions.quote: Avoid over — the counter medications (e.g., Milk of Magnesia may cause magnesium toxicity).

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with end-stage kidney disease has white crystals on the skin and severe itching. This is:
questions.rationale: Urea and urates crystallize on the skin in uremia, causing pruritus.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 15 Chronic renal failure (PDF p. 489)
questions.quote: Uremic frost. This is due to accumulation of urates in the skin.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How does the nurse check that a client's arteriovenous fistula is working?
questions.rationale: A palpable thrill and audible bruit show patency; avoid BP and needle sticks on that arm.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 15 Hemodialysis (PDF p. 492)
questions.quote: Assess for patency of AV fistula by auscultating for bruit and by palpating for thrill.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: During his first hemodialysis, a client develops headache, restlessness, nausea and confusion. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Wastes leave the blood faster than the brain, causing cerebral edema; first sessions are kept short to prevent it.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 15 Hemodialysis (PDF p. 492)
questions.quote: Disequilibrium syndrome is caused by more rapid removal of waste products from the blood than from the brain.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Before a hemodialysis session, the nurse usually holds which scheduled drug?
questions.rationale: Fluid removal lowers BP; antihypertensives are often held to prevent hypotension during dialysis.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 15 Hemodialysis (PDF p. 492)
questions.quote: Usually, antihypertensive medication doses are omitted during hemodialysis. To prevent hypotension.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Before instilling peritoneal dialysate, the nurse should:
questions.rationale: Warm dialysate improves comfort and clearance of wastes; additives are only as ordered.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 15 Peritoneal dialysis (PDF p. 492)
questions.quote: The dialysate solution should be warmed at body temperature.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Peritoneal dialysis outflow has slowed. The nurse first:
options: Turns the client side to side
questions.rationale: A loop of bowel may block the catheter; repositioning often restores flow.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 15 Peritoneal dialysis (PDF p. 492)
questions.quote: Ifthe drainage stops, turn the client to sides. The lumen of the catheter may be occluded by loop of colon.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on home peritoneal dialysis notices the drained fluid is cloudy. This suggests:
questions.rationale: Cloudy effluent indicates peritonitis; report it and send a sample for culture.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 15 Peritoneal dialysis (PDF p. 493)
questions.quote: Cloudy dialysate indicates peritonitis. Notify the physician. Collect specimen for culture.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on peritoneal dialysis has rising blood glucose. The reason is:
questions.rationale: Glucose in the dialysate is absorbed; monitor glucose and give insulin if prescribed.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 15 Peritoneal dialysis (PDF p. 493)
questions.quote: The dialysate solution contains glucose. Small doses of insulin may be required

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After a kidney transplant, a client on cyclosporine and prednisone is taught to:
options: Avoid crowds and people with infections
Stop the drugs once the kidney works
Take the drugs only when sick
questions.rationale: Immunosuppressants prevent rejection and are taken for life; they raise infection risk.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 15 Renal transplantation (PDF p. 493)
questions.quote: Protect the client from infection because these medications are immunosupressants.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with severe flank pain radiating to the groin and hematuria is being treated for a kidney stone. The nurse instructs him to:
questions.rationale: High fluid intake (about 3 L/day) and walking help pass the stone; strained stones go to the lab for analysis.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 15 Urinary calculi (PDF p. 494)
questions.quote: Strain all urine. Ifa stone is passed, submit it for laboratory analysis.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with calcium oxalate stones should limit:
questions.rationale: Spinach, tea, chocolate, nuts and beans are high in oxalate.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 15 Urinary calculi (PDF p. 494)
questions.quote: Avoid excess tea, chocolate, spinach (and other green leafy vegetables), almonds, cashew, beans.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A 65-year-old smoker has blood in his urine without pain. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Painless hematuria is the most characteristic sign of bladder cancer; smoking is the main risk factor.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 15 Bladder cancer (PDF p. 495)
questions.quote: The most characteristic manifestation of bladder cancer is painless hematuria.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with an ileal conduit asks how often urine will drain from the stoma. The nurse explains:
questions.rationale: An ileal conduit has no valve, so urine drains constantly and an appliance is always worn.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 15 Urinary diversion (PDF p. 495)
questions.quote: There is continuous outflow of urine from the stoma.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Sterile normal saline, not sterile water, is used for continuous bladder irrigation after TURP because it:
questions.rationale: Hypotonic fluid absorbed through open prostatic vessels can cause water intoxication; isotonic saline is used.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 15 Prostatectomy care (PDF p. 496)
questions.quote: Repeated administration of hypotonic solution e.g., sterile water, may cause water intoxication.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After prostatectomy, the client has a strong urge to void with the catheter in place. The nurse explains this is due to:
questions.rationale: Balloon pressure gives a sense of fullness; tell him not to strain or void around the catheter, which causes spasms and bleeding.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 15 Prostatectomy care (PDF p. 496)
questions.quote: This is due to pressure on the internal sphincter by the balloon of the catheter.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After catheter removal following prostatectomy, a client has dribbling of urine. The nurse teaches:
questions.rationale: Kegel (pelvic floor) exercises help regain urinary control.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 15 Prostatectomy care (PDF p. 496)
questions.quote: If dribbling of urine occurs, teach the client Kegel's exercise.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A woman who left a tampon in for 2 days now has high fever, a red rash, vomiting and low BP. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Retained blood-soaked packing or tampons allow S. aureus toxins to cause toxic shock syndrome.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 15 Toxic shock syndrome (PDF p. 497)
questions.quote: This is caused by blood — soaked packings like tampons, nasal packs, vaginal packs

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Oxybutynin is ordered for bladder spasms. The nurse checks first whether the client has:
questions.rationale: Oxybutynin is anticholinergic; it dilates pupils and can worsen glaucoma.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 15 Antispasmodics (PDF p. 494)
questions.quote: Do not administer these medications among clients with glaucoma.
